Modify a robot model

Source: R/robot-model.R
robot_modify.Rd

Models are immutable; these functions return modified copies. robot_add_frame() attaches a new massless frame (for example a tool center point) to an existing link through a fixed joint. robot_set_base() changes the pose of the root link in the world. robot_set_end_effector() changes the default end-effector frame. robot_set_inertia() replaces the inertial parameters of a link. robot_set_limits() replaces position limits of movable joints.

Usage

robot_add_frame(
  robot,
  name,
  parent,
  origin = robot_pose(),
  set_end_effector = TRUE
)

robot_set_base(robot, base)

robot_set_end_effector(robot, frame)

robot_set_inertia(
  robot,
  link,
  mass,
  com = c(0, 0, 0),
  inertia = matrix(0, 3, 3)
)

robot_set_limits(robot, limits)

Arguments

robot

A robot_model.

name

New frame name.

parent

Existing link to attach to.

origin

Pose of the new frame in the parent link frame.

set_end_effector

Make the new frame the default end effector.

base

New base pose.

frame

Frame name.

link

Link name.

mass, com, inertia

Inertial parameters as in robot_link().

limits

Matrix or list of c(lower, upper) with one entry per degree of freedom, or a named list keyed by joint name.

Value

A modified robot_model.

Examples

robot <- robot_example("planar2")
robot <- robot_add_frame(robot, "tcp", "link2", transl(0.1, 0, 0))
pose_translation(robot_fk(robot, c(0, 0)))
#> [1] 2.1 0.0 0.0
